parameters.name: market
parameters.description:
**Which national storefront to read.** Required.

One catalogue per country, each with its own merchants, cashback rates, coupons and category tree.
The market is chosen by this parameter alone  -  never by where the request comes from  -  so every
market is reachable from anywhere.

- `fr`  -  iGraal France
- `de`  -  Shoop Germany
- `pl`  -  iGraal Poland
- `es`  -  iGraal Spain

Long forms and the German brand name are accepted too: `france`, `germany`, `shoop`, `poland`,
`spain`. Call `/markets` for the live per-market merchant census.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
**Free-text merchant-name search.** Optional.

Matches on the merchant name, not the website  -  `nike` finds Nike, Nike By You and Nike Team
Sport, while `nike.com` finds nothing. To look a shop up by its domain use `website_url`
instead, which matches on the host.

- `nike`  -  Nike and related merchant entries in France
- `zalando`  -  the Zalando family (Zalando, Zalando Privé, Zalando Lounge, …)

An unmatched term returns an empty list with `total: 0`, not an error.

parameters.name: website_url

Matches on the host, so protocol, `www.`, trailing slash and path are all ignored and these

- `sosh.fr`  -  Sosh storefronts

parameters.name: category_ids
parameters.description:
**Restrict to one or more category ids.** Optional.

Ids are the UUIDs returned by `/categories`  -  both top-level categories and subcategories work.
Several ids are a union (OR): a merchant matching any of them is returned.

- `031f9caf-03b3-4a8f-b52a-7a476abe70c4`  -  Fashion & Accessories
- `75384eb3-272f-495f-bba8-d33158d1a106`  -  Electronics

A top-level id also matches merchants tagged only with its SUBcategories, so filtering by
"Broadband & Phone Contracts" returns the Broadband and Mobile Contracts merchants  -  but each
returned merchant's own `category_ids` lists the subcategory it carries, not the parent you
filtered on. That is expected, not a mismatch.

An id that does not exist yields `total: 0` rather than an error, so verify ids against
`/categories` before trusting an empty result. Comma-separated.

parameters.name: quality_positions
parameters.description:
**Restrict to merchants at given quality grades.** Optional. Numeric positions, not letters.

The platform grades every merchant, and the grade drives its own ranking. Several positions are
a union (OR). Full table at `/reference` (`merchant_qualities`):

- `1` AAA · `2` AA+ · `3` AA · `4` A+ · `5` A · `6` B · `7` C · `8` D · `9` E · `10` F

For example, `1,2` selects the two highest grades.

Every value must be a number  -  a non-numeric token is rejected with a `400` naming it, rather
than dropped (which would silently return the unfiltered catalogue). Comma-separated.

parameters.name: has_cashback
parameters.description:
**Only merchants with a live cashback campaign.** Optional  -  unset returns every merchant.

Use this to narrow a merchant catalogue to shops offering cashback.

- `true`  -  merchants carrying a campaign right now
- unset  -  no filtering on cashback

**`false` is rejected with a 400, deliberately.** There is no inverse filter: the catalogue
index narrows on `true` only, and a `false` would quietly return the whole catalogue under a
name that reads like the opposite. To count merchants without a campaign, subtract the
`has_cashback=true` total from the unfiltered total.

One caveat worth knowing: a merchant can pass this filter and still have no campaign that
resolves on `/cashback-rate`. The flag is a catalogue property and the campaign is a separate
record, so the two can disagree for a day.

parameters.name: next_token
parameters.description:
**Keyset cursor to resume the walk.** Optional  -  omit to start from the first merchant in the
catalogue.

Pass back, unchanged, the `next_token` from the previous response. The usual pattern is "call
once with no token, then keep passing back what you got until you stop". The token is opaque  - 
it is not a merchant id and nothing in your code should try to build, parse or edit one.

`has_more: false` (equivalently, a `null` `next_token` in the response) means there is no next
page  -  the walk has reached the end of the catalogue.

**A token this endpoint did not issue is refused with a `400`, on purpose.** The cursor carries
the market it belongs to and a checksum, so a stale, edited, hand-made or wrong-market token is
rejected with a message saying which of those it was. That matters more here than it looks: the
underlying position is a sorted merchant id, so a made-up but plausible token would otherwise
resume in the MIDDLE of the catalogue and silently skip every merchant before it  -  a bulk export
that quietly loses rows with nothing in the response to reveal it. Resuming is therefore either
exactly right or a clean error, never a silent short read.

all returns a `400`.

Every value must be a number; a non-numeric token is a `400` naming it rather than a silently
dropped id. Comma-separated.

moved over the life of a campaign.

because an ignored filter and an unfiltered call are indistinguishable in the response.

parameters.name: coupon_ids
parameters.description:
**Coupon ids to re-read, in one call.** Required  -  at least one id.

This is the direct-lookup door to a coupon you already hold. Everywhere else in the API the
coupon feed is reached through its filters  -  by merchant, by category, by expiry window  -  so a
stored id could be listed but never fetched back on its own. Pass it here and you get that exact
row again, in full.

The point is re-validation. A coupon saved yesterday may already be dead, and the returned row
answers that outright: `is_expired` and `ends_at` say whether the offer has run out,
`is_published` says whether it is still shown to shoppers, and `last_used_at` records the most
recent time a shopper actually redeemed it  -  the strongest freshness signal available, since a
code that worked minutes ago is far likelier to still work than one untouched for months.

- `021bd00a-7591-4e01-b6a7-e75f76088032`  -  one coupon (a live France code)
- `,,`  -  a whole saved wallet re-checked in a single call

Every coupon-returning endpoint echoes these ids as `id`, so collect them from `/coupons`,
`/merchant-coupons` or `/top-coupons` and store them alongside whatever you show your users.

Re-checking a saved wallet is a batch job, and a batch of ids is a single billable call instead of
one per coupon. Within a batch, an id that no longer resolves is simply left out of `coupons`,
so compare `count` against `requested_coupon_ids` to see which of your saved codes have dropped
out of the catalogue. A single id that does not resolve returns a 404 instead.

Ids are market-scoped: an id belonging to another national storefront is not found, so send the
`market` the coupon was originally read from. Comma-separated.

where `is_sponsored: true` on the response row means the brand is paying for the spot  -  it is the
only view into which merchants are buying promotion, and on which days, since spots rotate daily.

An unrecognised value is rejected with a `400` listing every accepted placement, rather than silently
returning nothing.

active_only.description:
**Only spots currently live.** Optional  -  default `true`.

Placements are scheduled: a spot has a `starts_at`/`ends_at` window and this flag filters on
it. Pass `false` to also see spots that are scheduled but not yet live, or that already
ended, which is useful for auditing a promotion calendar rather than rendering the live page.

- `true` (default)  -  only what a visitor would see right now
- `false`  -  every spot in the window, live or not

Be aware that `false` is a far heavier query  -  a single slot can hold hundreds of scheduled spots
(France `STICKY_BANNER`: 256 against 1 live). The busiest slots sometimes exceed the storefront's
own time budget; retry or use `active_only=true`.

limit.description:
**Maximum spots to return.** Optional  -  default `50`, maximum `200`.

The response always echoes the true `total` count of matching spots even when `limit` cuts the
`promotions` array short, so a caller can tell a slot was truncated rather than genuinely empty.

Ex: `50` (default), `200` (maximum).
